sections.text:
Zechariah, peace be upon him, is one of the righteous prophets of the Children of Israel. He worked as a carpenter and earned his living by working with his hands. He was a sponsor and educator of the Virgin Mary in Jerusalem.

Zechariah grew old, his head turned gray, his bones weakened, and his wife was barren and had not given birth to children since her youth.

Zechariah hoped that God would bless him with a good son who would inherit prophecy and knowledge and carry the banner of advocacy among the Children of Israel after him, for fear that the religion would be lost after his death.

One day, Zechariah entered upon Mary in her sanctuary, and found there the summer fruit in the winter, and the winter fruit in the summer!
He asked her in astonishment: “Oh Mary, how did this come to you?” She answered him with sincerity and certainty: “It is from God. Indeed, God provides for whomever He wills without reckoning.”

At that moment, Zechariah's heart was moved; The God who provided Mary with fruit outside of the season was able to provide her with a child outside of the time of childbearing (old age and infertility).

Zechariah turned to his Lord with a sincere, hidden appeal, and prayed to God, saying: “My Lord, grant me a good offspring from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Hearer of my supplication.”

God answered his prayer immediately, and the angels called him while he was standing praying in the sanctuary to give him the good news that God would bless him with a boy named “Yahya,” who had never given anyone this name before.

Zechariah was amazed and said: “Lord, how can I have a son when my wife is barren and I have reached old age?”

God answered him: “Thus said your Lord, ‘It is easy for me, and I created you before, and you were nothing.’”

Zechariah asked for a sign to reassure his heart, so God made his sign that he would not be able to speak to people for three days except by pointing, while remaining able to mention God and praise Him!
Zechariah went out to his people happily and advised them to praise God morning and evening.

Zechariah's barren wife became pregnant at menopause, and months passed until she gave birth to the blessed boy Yahya, completing the joy in the patient heart of the Prophet.

Yahya was born, the miracle was accomplished, and God confirmed the eye of Zachariah with his righteous son, who inherited prophecy and continued his father’s path in preaching and worship.

Zechariah made a great effort to raise Yahya and teach him the Torah and noble morals.

Zechariah's life was full of trials and patience. After Yahya grew up and became a prophet, the children of Israel confronted their prophets with rebellion and killing.

When Yahya was martyred, Zakaria was deeply saddened, and the attention of the tyrants turned to him as well.

They chased him into the forest, so Zechariah hid inside a tree that split for him by God’s command, but Satan guided them to him through the edge of his robe that remained outside the tree.

The tyrants sawed the tree with a saw, and Zechariah, peace be upon him, was martyred patiently and seeking reward to obtain the highest ranks of martyrdom before God.
